principles: Real host execution must be explicit opt-in, never implied by host availability alone.
Lattice remains authority-safe: local transcripts and receipts are evidence candidates, not production authority.
Claude Code first means Gemini/Codex behavior must not regress or silently become real subprocess execution.
Every real subprocess must be observable, bounded, cancellable, and reviewable from Lattice CLI.
drivers: User wants true Claude Code CLI execution after policy authorization, not only scaffold text.
Security boundary requires env filtering, cwd isolation, timeout, transcript capture, and manual merge.
Existing B-a5c2 dispatch_auto fake path and real-host refusal tests must remain deterministic and extend cleanly.

options.name: policy-bound-claude-real-runner
pros: Unlocks the requested Claude Code first real subprocess while preserving explicit user consent.
Minimizes blast radius by keeping Gemini/Codex scaffolded and keeping authority fields false.
Can be tested deterministically with a fake claude binary before live canary.
cons: Requires new policy field and runner metadata migration handling.
Subprocess lifecycle and cancellation add more implementation risk than scaffold-only flow.

options.name: manual-scaffold-only
pros: Lowest risk and matches existing tests.
No new subprocess or env surface.
cons: Does not satisfy the user request to let Lattice actually start Claude Code CLI.
Keeps Codex overflow story stuck at handoff guidance rather than execution.

options.name: all-real-hosts-at-once
pros: Would cover Claude/Gemini/Codex with one broad abstraction.
cons: Too much provider-specific uncertainty for one story.
Harder to test safely and more likely to overclaim unattended support.

rationale: Choose a Claude-only real runner gated by an explicit policy bit. This directly solves the requested user flow while keeping the host-neutral authority model intact and leaving Gemini/Codex unchanged until separately proven.

preMortem.trigger: Runner inherits full parent environment or logs env values
preMortem.consequence: Local credentials become persisted dispatch evidence
preMortem.mitigation: Build a minimal env from allowlist and safe basics, filter sensitive names, and record only env summaries without values.

preMortem.scenario: Claude process hangs or ignores prompt
preMortem.consequence: dispatch_auto never returns or leaves a zombie subprocess
preMortem.mitigation: Use policy maxRuntimeMinutes as child_process timeout, kill on timeout, set timedOut=true and failed status.

preMortem.trigger: Prompt or model writes files outside allowedPaths
preMortem.consequence: User may merge unbounded changes by mistake
preMortem.mitigation: Collect git changedFiles after run, compare with allowed/denied scope, fail or require review when scope violation exists.

preMortem.scenario: Local receipt is mistaken for production authority
preMortem.consequence: Story could appear DONE without independent authority
preMortem.mitigation: Keep authorityChanged=false, receiptVerified=false, productionDone=false and dispatch_merge_plan manualOnly=true in all paths.
